column1: A Quantitative Analysis of Inflation and Monetary Policy in Emerging Markets

The thesis titled Spillover Effects of US Monetary Policy on Emerging Markets Amidst Uncertainty by Povilas Lastauskas and Anh Dinh Minh Nguyen explores the impact of US monetary policy tightening on emerging markets  focusing on both direct and indirect spillover effects. Utilizing a global vector autoregression model with stochastic volatility across 32 countries  the study finds that an increase in US interest rates significantly reduces output in emerging markets  leading to more prolonged and persistent declines. This effect is exacerbated by global trade integration  which causes a sharper but slightly quicker rebounding output drop. The spillover effects are notably amplified when US monetary policy tightening coincides with increased monetary policy uncertainty. The research highlights the considerable heterogeneity in emerging markets' responses to US monetary policy shocks.

The paper begins by contextualizing the issue within the broader economic landscape  noting the challenges faced by emerging markets when the US Federal Reserve tightens monetary policy to combat inflation. This often results in a stronger US dollar  complicating the stability of local currencies and increasing macroeconomic uncertainty in emerging markets. The study emphasizes the global financial cycle  where US monetary policy shocks induce co-movements in international financial variables  affecting emerging markets even if they have weak direct links to the US.

The authors contribute to the literature by developing a global empirical macroeconometric model that covers nearly 90% of the world output  allowing for the quantification of direct and indirect impacts of US monetary policy changes on emerging markets. They also analyze the role of monetary policy uncertainty in global impacts when the Fed unexpectedly tightens monetary policy. The study is the first to quantify spillover strengths  both direct and indirect  while considering changes in policy and macroeconomic uncertainty.

The findings reveal that US monetary policy tightening reduces output growth and inflation  but also increases US macroeconomic volatility  particularly inflation volatility. The study underscores the importance of understanding both the direct and indirect channels through which US monetary policy affects emerging markets  highlighting the role of financial markets as a crucial transmission channel. The research provides valuable insights into the complex dynamics of international monetary policy transmission and the challenges faced by emerging markets in navigating these effects amidst uncertainty.
